lesson.title: My Florida B.E.S.T. Progress Map
lesson.topic: Track progress against Florida's B.E.S.T. standards for math and English language arts on a simple map the learner colors in.
lesson.steelman: Should a learning program follow the state's standards, or set its own goals?
lesson.steelman_for: Mapping to the state standards shows families and others clearly what a learner has covered and makes gaps easy to spot.
lesson.steelman_against: Standards are a floor, not the whole education; chasing checkboxes can crowd out deep projects and real curiosity.
lesson.example: Imagine Zara, 11, who prints the math standards for her grade, colors the ones she has mastered green and the ones in progress yellow, and picks a yellow one to work on this week.
lesson.activity: With a grown-up, open the official Florida B.E.S.T. standards list on CPALMS for your grade. Pick three math and three reading/writing standards. Make a chart: green = mastered, yellow = working on it, white = not started.
check_questions: What does a green box on your map mean?
Why might it help to see standards on one page?
What is one thing standards cannot measure?
